Package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.widgets

Class CalendarEvent

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.rest.server.widgets.CalendarEvent
public class CalendarEvent extends Object
A single calendar event — also the element type of the per-month event GET envelope's events.

Bean-only (juneau-rest-server-widgets): the emitter and runtime live in juneau-rest-server-views. Titles, tooltips, and labels are painted with textContent by the runtime, never as markup.

end is layout-significant, with split inclusivity:
  • All-day (date-only end): inclusive. start=2026-03-02, end=2026-03-04 occupies three day cells.
  • Timed (date-time end): exclusive. start=…T09:00, end=…T10:00 occupies [09:00, 10:00) — the start day only. A timed event crossing midnight is a spanning bar using the exclusive end, never intra-day chips on each crossed day.
  • Omitted end: start-only, and valid. An all-day event occupies the start day cell; a timed event occupies the start instant as a zero-width chip on the start day (never a spanning bar).
  • An all-day end equal to start is a single-day event; a timed end equal to start is zero-duration and is rejected, as is any end before start.
All-day agreement and the malformed set:

Agreement between allDay and the shape of end is decided by effectiveAllDay(), never by the raw allDay field, so a null allDay paired with matching start/end shapes stays valid. An event is malformed for exactly these reasons — and no others:

  1. a missing/blank id, title, or start;
  2. an unparseable start/end civil date, or an end that is not after (all-day: not on or after) start;
  3. a declared allDay/end disagreement — allDay == true with a date-time end, or allDay == false with a date-only end;
  4. mixed start/end shapes with a null allDay.

A malformed event is dropped by CalendarDef.validate() and by a per-month GET handler that filters through retainWellFormed(Collection) — the same rule on both paths. Neither fails the whole definition nor the whole month payload. An omitted end is not malformed.

Timezone contract:

start/end are interpreted as an ISO-8601 local date (yyyy-MM-dd) or local date-time (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm). A trailing offset or Z is fail-soft ignored, never rejected — a seeded 2026-03-02T09:00:00Z keeps validating and keeps rendering at 09:00 in the server's injected clock zone. The same parse applies on the seed path and on the per-month GET path.

Since:
10.0.0

    • civilEnd

      public LocalDate civilEnd()
      The civil date of end, or null when end is omitted.

      This is the raw civil date of the bound, before inclusivity is applied — use lastDay() for the last day cell the event actually occupies.

      Returns:
      The civil end date, or null when end is omitted or blank.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If end is present but not a parseable ISO date/date-time.

    • lastDay

      public LocalDate lastDay()
      The last day cell this event occupies, applying the split inclusivity rule (see the class javadoc).

      Equals civilStart() when end is omitted. For an all-day event the date-only end is inclusive; for a timed event the date-time end is exclusive, so an end of exactly midnight lands on the previous day. Never earlier than civilStart().

      Returns:
      The inclusive last occupied day.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If start/end are not parseable.

    • malformedReason

      public String malformedReason()
      The reason this event is malformed, or null when it is well-formed.

      This is the single drop predicate shared by CalendarDef.validate() (the seed path) and by retainWellFormed(Collection) (the per-month GET path); see the class javadoc for the complete, closed list of malformed reasons. It is a pure shape check: an unknown categoryId, an unsafe href, and an off-month start are author errors reported by validate(Set,Integer,Integer), not drop reasons.

      Returns:
      A human-readable reason, or null when this event is well-formed.

    • retainWellFormed

      public static List<CalendarEvent> retainWellFormed(Collection<CalendarEvent> values)
      Returns the well-formed events of the given collection, dropping the malformed ones and continuing.

      A per-month GET handler filters its payload through this before serialization so the dynamic path drops exactly what CalendarDef.validate() drops on the seed path. A null element is dropped too.

      Parameters:
      values - The events to filter. May be null.
      Returns:
      A new mutable list of the well-formed events, in the original order. Never null.

    • validate

      public void validate(Set<String> knownCategoryIds, Integer initialYear, Integer initialMonth)
      Fail-closed shape check for a seed event, reused by CalendarDef.validate() and by an endpoint handler that wants to validate its own payload before serialization.

      Throws for a malformed event (see malformedReason()) and for the author errors a seed definition must not contain: an undeclared categoryId, a cross-origin href, and a start outside the rendered window. Callers that want the drop-and-continue posture of the seed and per-month GET paths use malformedReason()/retainWellFormed(Collection) instead.

      Parameters:
      knownCategoryIds - The declared category ids; a set categoryId must be a member. May be null (then any categoryId fails).
      initialYear - The initial year the seed month is rendered for, or null to skip the off-month check.
      initialMonth - The 1-based initial month, or null to skip the off-month check.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If this event is not well-formed.
